statement: The Ugaritic Baal Cycle presents Baal/Hadad within a storm-and-divine-war repertoire that includes kingship, conflict with Sea/Yamm, and storm imagery; this repertoire supplies the comparative baseline for later Yahwistic appropriation claims.

sources.citation: Mark S. Smith, The Ugaritic Baal Cycle, vol. II (Brill, 2009).
sources.author: Mark S. Smith
sources.access_note: Bibliographic preview and contents confirm the work's treatment of Baal, Yamm, cloud-rider language, kingship, and the Ugaritic narrative cycle.

sources.citation: David Noel Freedman and C. Franke Hyland, “Psalm 29: A Structural Analysis,” Harvard Theological Review 66 (1973): 237–256.
sources.author: David Noel Freedman; C. Franke Hyland
sources.access_note: Cambridge extract summarizes Canaanite storm-god/Baal elements used as the comparative background for Psalm 29.

does_not_demonstrate: This does not establish direct literary borrowing from the surviving Ugaritic tablets into a biblical text.
Storm-god motifs are not unique to Ugarit, so specific transmission claims require additional evidence.
